name: percentage-table
title: Percentage table (benchmark ladder)
tagline: Of-amount percentage benchmark ladder (100% = amount, then 50% / 10% / 5% / 1% …); each value derived, ÷k/×k mental-step arrows, and a build-up to a target %.
description: A single-quantity of-amount benchmark ladder, drawn as a two-column table: a Percentage column (100%, 50%, 25%, 20%, 10%, 5%, 1% …) and a value column headed "of <amount>". You write one original amount (the 100% whole) and which benchmark percents to list; the model derives each row's value (percent/100 × amount, exact), the ÷k / ×k scale-factor arrows between consecutive rows (the mental step — halve, ÷10), and, if you give a `build`, a foot row that combines chosen benchmarks into a target percentage ("35% = 3 × 10% + 5%") with its derived value. Occlude any row's value to "?" for "find 10% of the amount", occlude a percent for the reverse "what percentage is this?", blank cells for a staged build, and highlight the rows that matter. Values format as plain numbers, or as money (`prefix: "£"`, pence shown only when present) or with a `suffix` unit. The tabular benchmark cousin of mental-percent methods — distinct from fdp-table (equivalence of one value) and ratio-table (scaling a multi-part ratio).
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a percentage of an amount is found by benchmarks or mental %: "find 10% / 5% / 1% of £600", the build-up method (find 10% then 5%, add them for 15%; find 1% then multiply), halving for 50% and 25%, and complete-the-ladder questions. Author the semantics: set `amount` (the 100% whole, the problem's given), then `benchmarks` — the percent rows in the order you want them read (default 100, 50, 10, 5, 1). The value of each row is computed; you never write one. Order matters because the ÷k/×k arrow between two consecutive rows is derived from their percents — list 100, 50, 25 to show "halve, halve again"; list 100, 10, 1 to show "÷10, ÷10"; list 10, 5 to show "halve 10% for 5%". To pose a question: set a benchmark's `occlude` to hide its value ("find 10% of 600"), `occludePercent` to hide its percent (the reverse, "60 is what % of 600?"), or `show.values: false` for a blank answer-space ladder (the percents and arrows stay as the method). For the build-up, add a `build` with `parts` (the benchmarks combined, each with an optional `times`): the model derives the target percent (the sum) and its value and draws a foot row plus a "35% = 3 × 10% + 5%" working line; set `build.occlude` to hide the target value ("find 35% of 600" — the visible benchmark rows are the scaffold). Highlight the benchmark rows a build draws from so pupils see which ones are added. Money: set `prefix: "£"` (or `money: true`) and values show pence only when needed (£60, £3.65). `suffix` adds a unit (" ml", " g"). Cross-block convention: keep the same amount and the same benchmark set across one lesson so pupils track one ladder; change only what is occluded, built or asked. Strongly staged: open on the 100% row, bring in one benchmark (with its arrow) per stage; or open on the ladder, highlight the rows to add, then reveal the build foot row last — the base (the 100% row, or the bare ladder) stands alone as a sensible figure. Switch model when the teaching is percentage change / a multiplier / reverse percentage (use number/percentage-square or number/compound-growth-table), or fraction↔decimal↔percentage equivalence (use number/fdp-table), or scaling a multi-part ratio (use number/ratio-table). Synonyms a teacher might use: percentage of an amount, percent of, find 10%, 1% method, benchmark percentages, build up, mental percentages, halve for 50%, complete the table, of amount.

amount.description: The whole quantity = 100%. The single ORIGINAL authored value; every benchmark value is derived from it. Write the amount from the problem (600, 80, 240, 2.5). For money use it with `prefix: "£"`.

items.description: One benchmark percentage = one ROW of the ladder, top to bottom. Its `value` (this percent of the amount) is always derived; list flags here only to occlude, blank or highlight it. Order the rows so consecutive arrows show the mental step you want (100, 50, 25 for halving; 100, 10, 1 for the ÷10 method).

percent.description: The percentage for this row — a number, NOT a string ("%" is added for you). 100 is the whole amount; 50, 25, 20, 10, 5, 1 are the usual benchmarks; 2.5 and 12.5 are fine. Its value (percent/100 × amount) is computed.

occlude.description: Render this row's VALUE as "?" — the "find this percentage of the amount" hook. The percent stays visible; the hidden value appears nowhere else (cell, arrow, build, aria) so it cannot leak. Default false.

occludePercent.description: Render this row's PERCENT as "?" — the REVERSE hook ("this value is what percentage of the amount?"). The value stays visible. The arrows touching this row read "÷ ?" so the percent cannot leak. Default false.

blank.description: Render this row's value cell EMPTY (nothing) — an unfilled row, for a staged build that fills the ladder one row at a time, or a per-row answer space. Different from occlude: "?" poses a question, blank poses nothing yet. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this whole row (percent + value) — the benchmark in focus, a row being combined in a build-up, or the answer row. Default false.

benchmarks.description: The benchmark percentage rows of the ladder, top to bottom. Default [100, 50, 10, 5, 1] if omitted. Order them so the consecutive arrows show the mental route you want (see whenToUse).

build.description: Add a build-up foot row that combines benchmarks into a target percentage. OMIT for a plain ladder. The target percent (Σ percent × times) and its value are derived; a "target% = a% + b% …" working line is drawn beneath the table.

items.description: One benchmark used in the build-up, optionally taken several times. "30% = 3 × 10% + 5%" is parts [{ percent: 10, times: 3 }, { percent: 5 }].

percent.description: The benchmark percentage being added (usually one that appears as a row above).

times.description: How many of this benchmark are added — renders "3 × 10%". Default 1.

parts.description: The benchmarks added together, left to right. [{ percent: 10, times: 3 }, { percent: 5 }] builds 35%. Usually these percents also appear as rows above (the scaffold).

occlude.description: Render the target VALUE as "?" — "find this percentage of the amount". The percent build and the visible benchmark rows stay as the scaffold. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the build foot row — answer emphasis. Default false.

prefix.description: Text put BEFORE every value — a currency symbol, usually "£". With "£" (or `money: true`) values show pence only when present (£60, £3.65). Omit for none.

suffix.description: Text put AFTER every value — a unit, e.g. " ml", " g", " cm". Omit for none.

money.description: Format values as money: show 2 decimal places only when there are pence (£60, £3.65 — never £60.00). Set automatically when `prefix` is "£". Default false.

arrows.description: Show the scale-factor arrows between consecutive rows (the mental step: ÷2, ÷10, ×5). Default true. Only drawn when there are at least two rows.

arrowStyle.description: "split" (default): the multiplier on the LEFT going down and its inverse on the RIGHT going up (÷2 down, ×2 up — "there and back"). "both": the SAME multiplier on both edges, both arrows pointing down.

factors.description: Show the numeric multiplier on each arrow. Default true. Set false to pose "what is the step?" — the arrows read "÷ ?" / "× ?".

values.description: Show every derived value. Default true. Set false for a blank answer-space ladder: the percents, headers and arrows stay (the method), and every derived value blanks for pupils to fill — EXCEPT the 100% row, which keeps its value (that is the given whole, the anchor). The build target value blanks too. Blank the 100% row explicitly if you want it empty as well.

headers.description: Show the column-header row ("Percentage" and "of <amount>"). Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the table; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the table, e.g. a stem sentence ("10% of £600 is £60, so halve it for 5%"). Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

params.caption: Halve 100% for 50%; take a tenth for 10%; halve that for 5%; a tenth of 10% is 1%.
